title: With The Bard Out To Pasture, It's Finally Time To Have Fun; Bartholomew Fair

contact_edits.before: There's satisfying work from Jonathan Goad as a gambling gallant who loses one heiress and gets another, older but richer (note that, in a comedy without a love story, he's the closest thing to a hero); from Randy Hughson and Victor Ertmanis as a pair of pimps who put a couple of respectable women on the game, right under their husbands' noses; from Jesse Aaron Dwyer as a conscientious cutpurse; Michael Spencer-Davis in the minute role of an officer; and Cliff Saunders who runs a great puppet-show. The show itself is a production highlight, and though some of the fairground jollity is run-of-the-mill, there is also some good surprise staging and an unusually intelligent placing of actors in the auditorium. Jonsonian comedy, combining a thick text with the action of a farce, is a tough act; this is an encouraging start at cracking it. - Bartholomew Fair is in repertory through Oct. 2. Call 1-800-567-1600 or visit stratfordfestival.cafor tickets and information.
